caveats: Eight of the ten are micro-practices (sole CPA or one-lawyer offices) with no website, so the realistic engagement is a small site plus a Google Business Profile cleanup, not a deep AI programme - and budgets are correspondingly small.

Google ratings and review counts were read from the live Maps place panel where it rendered, otherwise from a TaxScout/Birdeye mirror that republishes Google's figures with a date; two entries (K Y Tapya, Molnar Revilla) showed a star value with no review count, so treat those as low-confidence.
Only one business in the batch (Ibrahim Injury Law) has a website to review as a customer, so website scores elsewhere reflect total absence, not poor design.

Spelling of some business names differs between the batch, the directories and the Google listing (e.g. 'Englehardt Simon Accounting & Tax Services' vs 'Simon Englehardt Accounting'); I matched on address and phone.
The find-open.com source pages in batch.json were treated as the candidate list only; every business was re-checked against Google and at least one other source.
data_gaps: Google review text was mostly not readable: the Maps panel served a limited view, so review-complaint analysis (missed calls, slow replies) could not be done beyond the one visible Englehardt review.
No firm had published price ranges, and none had any online booking, so 'bookable' is 0 for nine of ten.
Could not confirm whether vrevillacpa.com belongs to the Molnar Revilla practice - the site names New York and never mentions East Brunswick or Molnar.
Operating status of Samuel H. Davis and Carl A. Marczak, PC could not be confirmed either way (no live Google listing, no reachable phone on a live page); no calls were made, per the read-only rule.
Whether K Y Tapya's and Richard Uslan's Google profiles are formally claimed is inferred from the absence of a 'Claim this business' prompt, not confirmed.
